newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo aluminium recovers ground on yen's plunge.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo aluminium recovers ground on yen's plunge.

text.p: The Tokyo aluminium futures market closed higher on Tuesday, recovering earlier losses, due to the yen's plunge against the dollar, local traders said.

Prices were 0.2 to 1.5 yen higher, with the benchmark February 1998 contract up 0.5 yen at 205.6 yen per kg. The day's volume was 8,290 lots, sharply down from 19,645 lots on Monday which was the first trading day.

All contracts opened lower after a slide in the London Metal Exchange (LME) three-month aluminium price overnight, but the yen's plunge triggered buying orders from local investors later, traders said.
The dollar surged to 126.00 yen on Tuesday afternoon in Tokyo, against around 124.70 yen late on Monday afternoon.

"Today's key factor was the yen's fall," an aluminium trader at a major trade house said. "But liquidity is still low, and we can't do active arbitrage trading between Tokyo and the physical market yet," he said.

Traders said the dive in Japanese aluminium futures on Monday clearly affected the overseas market overnight. "But today's lower volume indicates the Tokyo market still has a long way to go," another aluminium trader said.
The aluminium contract on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange is the first base metal futures contract ever traded in Japan.
